Operator:
Good day, and welcome to the Nimbus Cloud Technologies Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in listen-only mode. After the presentation, we will conduct a question-and-answer session. To ask a question, you will need to register using the *1 and *2 keys. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Chen, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Chen:
Good afternoon, everyone, and thank you for joining us. Today, we will be discussing Nimbus Cloud Technologies' results for the third quarter of fiscal 2024. With me on the call are Alex Rivera, Chief Executive Officer; Jordan Lee, Chief Financial Officer; and Taylor Kim, Chief Technology Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that today's call contains forward-looking statements. These statements are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of these risks.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Alex Rivera.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, Sarah, and good afternoon, everyone. Thank you for joining us today. Nimbus Cloud had a strong Q3, driven by continued growth in our cloud platform and increasing adoption of our AI-powered services.

During the quarter, we focused on four key areas:
1. Expanding our global infrastructure.
2. Enhancing our platform security.
3. Driving innovation in AI and machine learning.
4. Strengthening our partnerships.

Let me dive deeper into the explosive growth in AI and machine learning workloads, which continues to be the brightest spot in our business. This isn't just a trend—it's a structural shift reshaping the entire cloud computing landscape, and we're right at the epicenter.

The numbers speak for themselves. In Q3, AI/ML-related revenue grew 48% year-over-year, accelerating from 42% in Q2, and now represents 28% of our total Infrastructure-as-a-Service revenue—up from just 18% a year ago. This growth is underpinned by a 62% YoY increase in AI/ML compute hours consumed across our platform, driven primarily by our next-generation GPU and TPU offerings. Remaining Performance Obligations tied to AI/ML commitments surged 75% YoY to $4.2 billion, signaling strong multi-year demand. On adoption, 68% of our top 1,000 enterprise customers are now actively running AI/ML workloads—up from 52% last year—with net new adopters adding another 15% quarter-over-quarter. That's outpacing the broader cloud market, where Gartner estimates industry-wide AI/ML adoption at around 45% for hyperscale providers.

Breaking it down by workload type, we're seeing the classic bifurcation defining the AI era. Training workloads, which dominated early post-ChatGPT hype, grew 35% YoY but now account for only 38% of total AI/ML compute—down from 55% last year—as customers optimize for efficiency with techniques like LoRA fine-tuning and mixture-of-experts architectures. Inference, however, exploded 82% YoY and now comprises 62% of our AI/ML hours. This shift is fueled by real-time applications: low-latency Retrieval-Augmented Generation pipelines for customer service bots and edge-deployed vision models in autonomous systems. Our inference-optimized instances, like the NCasT4_v5 series powered by NVIDIA H100s and our proprietary Neuron accelerators—delivering 20% better token-per-dollar efficiency than comparable offerings—have been key enablers here, with utilization rates hitting 92% during peak hours thanks to our advanced multi-tenancy scheduler.

From a technical standpoint, we've made massive strides to stay ahead. In Q3, we brought online 15 new AI-optimized zones across our global regions, expanding H100 cluster capacity by 3.5x to over 50,000 GPUs. This includes our new A3 Ultra instances, benchmarked at 2.1x the performance of A100s on MLPerf training suites for Stable Diffusion workloads. On the software side, our NexAI Studio platform saw 110% YoY growth in active users, with seamless integrations to Hugging Face Transformers, LangChain, and Ray for distributed training. We've also rolled out zero-ETL data pipelines with Apache Iceberg support, slashing time-to-model from weeks to hours for customers migrating from on-prem Hadoop clusters. And sustainability matters: our AI workloads now run on 85% carbon-free energy in eligible regions, aligning with enterprise ESG mandates.

Regionally, the story is equally compelling. North America remains our powerhouse, contributing 55% of AI/ML growth with 52% YoY expansion, led by media giants fine-tuning LLMs like Llama 3 on our platform for personalized content recommendation. EMEA grew 45% YoY, bolstered by GDPR-compliant federated learning for healthcare, where we've won deals running differential privacy on our TPU v5p pods. APAC is the fastest at 68% YoY, driven by semiconductor and manufacturing AI; Japan and South Korea alone added $450 million in RPO from chipmakers optimizing fab processes with reinforcement learning, despite U.S. export controls creating some elasticity in HBM supply chains. China growth moderated to 22% due to local data sovereignty regs, but we're gaining share via partnerships with hybrid cloud setups.

Strategically, this positions us uniquely. Unlike pure-play GPU resellers, our full-stack approach—compute, storage with 99.999999999% durability, and 800Gbps RDMA over Converged Ethernet networking—delivers 25-30% lower total cost of ownership versus fragmented alternatives. We've deepened our NVIDIA alliance with early DGX Cloud access and are piloting AMD MI300X for cost-sensitive inference, while investing $2.5 billion in FY24 capex for custom silicon. Customer wins underscore this: a Fortune 50 bank scaled fraud detection models to 10 petaFLOPS, reducing false positives by 40%; a stealth GenAI startup hit $100 million ARR in six months on our platform; and automotive OEMs are deploying vision transformers for Level 4 autonomy at the edge.

Looking forward, we expect AI/ML to drive 50-55% of our IaaS growth in FY24, with Q4 acceleration as inference scales post-holiday model releases. RPO conversion remains strong at 45% for the back half, and we're guiding for $1.8-2.0 billion in AI/ML net new ARR. Capacity constraints are minimal—we've locked in supply through 2025 via forward commitments.

In short, AI/ML isn't a bubble; it's the new workloads layer of the cloud stack, and we're executing flawlessly to capture it.

Now I'll turn the call over to Jordan to discuss our financial results in more detail.

Jordan Lee:
Thank you, Alex. As Alex mentioned, we had a strong financial performance in the Q3. Revenue grew by 28% year-over-year to $30.5 billion. Our gross margin was 78%, and our operating margin was 32%.

I'll now turn to our Q3 and full-year fiscal 2024 outlook, with a particular focus on our Cloud segment, which continues to be the growth engine for Nimbus Cloud Technologies. We reported Q3 Cloud revenue of $27.8 billion, up 30% year-over-year and 9% quarter-over-quarter, driven by robust demand for our AI/ML workloads, sovereign cloud offerings, and elastic compute capacity. This represented 91% of our total Q3 revenue of $30.5 billion, which grew 28% year-over-year.

Looking ahead, we are guiding Q4 Cloud segment revenue to $29.5 billion to $30.2 billion, implying 32% to 36% year-over-year growth at the midpoint. This reflects continued strength across our core pillars: IaaS expected to grow 30% YoY, PaaS at 37% YoY fueled by our NexAI platform, and high-margin SaaS and data services up 27% YoY. Our Annual Recurring Revenue ended Q3 at $105 billion, up 34% YoY, with Remaining Performance Obligations at a record $195 billion, up 44% YoY, signaling strong multi-year visibility.

For the full company in Q4, we expect total revenue of $32.3 billion to $33.0 billion, representing 27% to 31% YoY growth. This incorporates growth in our Enterprise Software segment, which should contribute $2.5 billion to $2.6 billion, up 14% YoY, as we cross-sell cloud-native integrations.

Shifting to full-year FY2024 guidance, we are raising our Cloud segment outlook to $114 billion to $118 billion, a 32% to 37% increase over FY2023's $86.2 billion. Full-year company revenue is now guided at $125 billion to $129 billion, up 29% to 33% YoY, with Cloud comprising over 91% of the mix.

Let me break this down by key drivers and regional dynamics, underscoring the durability of our trajectory in a market IDC projects to grow at 21% CAGR through 2027.

Generative AI remains the accelerant. In Q3, AI-related revenue—spanning our NexAI foundation models, Triton Inference Server, and GPU-accelerated clusters—surpassed $8.5 billion, up 65% YoY. We're guiding Q4 AI revenue to $10 billion to $10.5 billion, with full-year AI at 26% to 28% of Cloud mix. Initiatives like Project Nebula, optimizing LLM fine-tuning with 40% lower TCO via custom NitroTPU chips and Ray-based orchestration, are landing hyperscale deals, including net-new commitments from a major U.S. automaker migrating 50,000 H100-equivalent workloads and a European telco building private GenAI instances on our sovereign zones.

Regionally:
- Americas (55% of Cloud mix): Q4 growth of 34% YoY, anchored by enterprise migrations. We've secured $16 billion in multi-year contracts, including expansions with Fortune 100 names.
- EMEA (25% mix): 30% YoY growth in Q4, offset by sovereign cloud ramps in France and the UK. Our Paris and Frankfurt zones added 20% more capacity.
- APAC (20% mix): 40% YoY Q4 growth, driven by data localization in India and Indonesia. Our Mumbai and Jakarta regions saw 50% capacity utilization uplift from workloads fleeing on-prem environments.

We're navigating a multi-cloud world adeptly—47% of our top 1,000 customers run hybrid/multi setups, with our interoperability layer boosting stickiness. Cost optimization tools have driven 16% YoY improvement in customer price-performance, aiding 98% dollar-based net retention. Capex remains disciplined at 18% of revenue for FY2024, funding 25 new Availability Zones and sustainable data centers targeting 100% renewable energy by 2028.

Risks to guide include FX volatility—assuming a stronger USD—and supply chain constraints on high-end GPUs, though our diversified sourcing mitigates this. Overall, we're positioned to outpace the market, gaining share in a $700 billion-plus TAM.

Now, I'll hand it back to Alex for further comments.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, Jordan. We are particularly excited about the momentum we are seeing with NexAI Studio, which is driving significant adoption and efficiency gains for our customers.

Good afternoon, everyone. Before we open the floor to questions, I'd like to dive deeper into one of the key macroeconomic factors influencing our results this quarter: the impact of currency fluctuations on our revenue. As a global leader in cloud infrastructure and platform services—much like our peers—we derive over 65% of our revenue from international markets. This exposure introduces volatility from foreign exchange movements. Let me break this down with specifics on the headwinds we faced, regional drivers, our mitigation strategies, and our forward outlook.

In Q3, reported revenue came in at $30.5 billion, up 26% year-over-year on a reported basis. However, on a constant currency basis—excluding the impact of FX—this would have been 30% growth, representing a 400 basis point headwind from currency fluctuations. That's a $1.2 billion drag on top-line revenue for the quarter alone. For the full year to date, FX has shaved approximately 3.5 percentage points off our year-over-year growth rate, equating to a cumulative $3.8 billion in foregone revenue when benchmarked against constant currency figures.

The U.S. dollar strengthened by an average of 7% against our basket of reporting currencies during the quarter, driven by the Federal Reserve's hawkish stance amid persistent inflation and resilient U.S. economic data. The Bloomberg Dollar Index rose 5.2% quarter-over-quarter. This isn't unique to us; peers cited similar 300-400 bps FX headwinds.

Breaking it down regionally across our IaaS, PaaS, and SaaS workloads:
- EMEA (38% of total revenue): Largest hit at $760 million—or 63%—of the quarterly headwind. The euro depreciated 8.1% against the USD. Our EMEA business grew 28% on constant currency, fueled by sovereign cloud and GPU instances for GenAI, but the weakening pound added pressure from UK public sector deals.
- APAC (20% of revenue): $310 million headwind, driven by a 12% plunge in the Japanese yen and Australian dollar softening. Constant currency growth was 35%, thanks to hyperscale expansions.
- LATAM and Other Emerging Markets (7% of revenue): $140 million impact, with Brazilian real down 6%. Growth was 31% constant currency.

North America, at 35% of revenue, grew 18% YoY with no FX exposure.

Our revenue model—70% consumption-based—is somewhat insulated due to monthly rebilling and high stickiness (net revenue retention at 125%). However, translation exposure affects consolidated results.

Historically, FY2022 had a 2.5% tailwind; FY2023 neutral; FY2024 a 3-4% headwind. If DXY holds above 105 into 2025, another 200-300 bps drag.

Our FX risk management includes:
1. Natural hedges (60% coverage): Billing in local currencies, matching expenses.
2. Financial hedges: 70-80% of forecasted exposure hedged, capturing $420 million in gains in Q3.
3. Pricing discipline: Dynamic adjustments boosting ARPU by 5% YoY.
4. Technical initiatives: Automated currency conversion and stablecoin pilots.

Looking forward, Q4 reported growth of 27-29%, constant currency 31-33%. Our $195 billion RPO provides visibility.

In summary, FX headwinds masked underlying momentum, but constant currency underscores our cloud-native strength.

We continue to invest in research and development to stay ahead of the curve in the rapidly evolving cloud landscape. Our commitment to innovation is reflected in our recent advancements in A3 Ultra instances.

Thank you, Jordan, and good afternoon, everyone. As we wrap up Q3 results, I'd like to address the expected impact of macroeconomic factors on our full-year outlook and into FY25. While we've seen persistent headwinds from elevated interest rates, moderating inflation, and recessionary fears—particularly in enterprise IT budgets—our cloud-first model positions us resiliently. Cloud's opex advantages have accelerated migrations, with 68% of our top 100 customers now running over 70% of workloads on our platform, up from 52% a year ago.

Breaking it down by key macro drivers:

Interest rates and cost optimization: The Fed's terminal rate around 5.25-5.50% has prolonged capex scrutiny, with Gartner estimating 7-10% YoY contraction in global IT spend. This is a tailwind for us: our mainframe modernization via QuantumShift saw 45% QoQ bookings ramp, yielding 3x TCO savings. We expect this to offset SMB churn, with DBNER at 118% in Q3, guiding 115-120% for FY24.

Inflation and supply chain: Core PCE at 2.7% eased GPU costs down 15% QoY. Energy prices up 12% in EMEA pressuring PUE, but GreenCloud liquid-cooled racks improved efficiency 25%, keeping gross margins at 78-80%.

Recession risks and geopolitics: 35% U.S. recession odds for H1 2025 weigh on spend, but RPO grew 28% YoY to $195 billion, 85% multi-year. U.S.-China restrictions boost sovereign cloud in APAC; certifications unlock public sector.

Regionally:
- Americas (62%): 24% YoY FY24 growth, led by GenAI.
- EMEA (22%): 7-9% growth guide.
- APAC (16%): 32%+ growth.

Macro tailwinds from AI supercycle outweigh headwinds. Capex $5.5 billion (18% of revenue) for new capacity and Nexus Fabric interoperability. Cost-optimization renewed 92% of contracts.

While we guide FY24 revenue at $125-129 billion (29-33% YoY), FY25 accelerates to 24-27%. Free cash flow $20-22 billion, ROIC 28%.

With that, let's open the call for questions.

Operator:
Ladies and gentlemen, instructions for the Q&A session. Our first question comes from John Smith with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

John Smith:
Thanks, and congrats on the quarter. Alex, on the AI/ML side, with such strong inference growth and capacity expansions, can you talk more about supply chain risks for GPUs into next year and how you're diversifying?

Alex Rivera:
Thanks, John. Great question. As we highlighted, we've locked in supply through 2025 with forward commitments from NVIDIA and are piloting AMD MI300X for inference to diversify. Our $2.5 billion capex for custom silicon further de-risks us, and with utilization at 92%, we're managing demand efficiently without constraints. This full-stack approach keeps us ahead.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Maria Lopez with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Maria Lopez:
Hi team, solid guidance raise. Jordan, how are you factoring macro headwinds like rates and recession risks into the FY24 and FY25 outlooks, especially with the tempered EMEA growth?

Jordan Lee:
Thanks, Maria. We've baked in a 2-point macro drag for FY24, reflecting IT spend caution, but AI tailwinds more than offset via 115-120% DBNER. For FY25, we see acceleration to 24-27% as rates ease. RPO visibility at $195 billion, with regional balance—APAC strong, EMEA offset by sovereign wins—gives confidence. Capex discipline at 18% supports this.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Raj Patel with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Raj Patel:
Thanks. Taylor, impressive strides in NexAI Studio and zero-ETL pipelines. Can you elaborate on how these integrations with Hugging Face and Ray are impacting developer adoption and competitive differentiation?

Taylor Kim:
Absolutely, Raj. NexAI Studio's 110% user growth comes from seamless tools like Hugging Face Transformers for model deployment and Ray for scaling distributed training across our 50,000+ GPUs. Zero-ETL with Iceberg cuts migration time dramatically, differentiating us with 20% better efficiency than peers. This drives 68% top-customer adoption, fueling inference explosion.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Emily Chen with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Emily Chen:
Great results. On FX, that's a hefty headwind—how sustainable are your hedging gains, and any pricing actions planned for high-volatility regions like APAC and LATAM?

Alex Rivera:
Thanks, Emily. Our layered hedging—natural offsets, 70-80% financial coverage—delivered $420 million gains in Q3, muting impact. Pricing discipline with dynamic spot adjustments and geo-surcharges lifted ARPU 5% without churn. For APAC/LATAM, stablecoin pilots and local billing will further insulate as we expand in India and UAE.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you for your questions and your continued support. We are confident in our ability to continue to deliver strong results and create long-term value for our shareholders.

Sarah Chen:
Thank you for joining us today. This concludes the call.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
